summary: The root هوي (hwy) primarily signifies falling or descending, often implying a downward motion or a plunge.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: هَوَى بِهِ He made it to fall down: see an ex. in a verse of Ru-beh, cited voce رِياَغٌ, in art. ريغ. See 4. هَوَتْ أُ ُنُهُ His ears heard a confused, or humming, or singing, sound. (K.) هَوَتْ أُمُّهُ is used to express wonder; like as when one says, قَاتَلَهُ ٱللّٰهُ مَا أَسْمَعَهُ. (IB, in TA, art. ام.)

أَهْوَى إِلَى الشَّىْءِ بِيَدِهِ He extended, or stretched forth, his arm, or hand, to the thing to take it; it being near: if it be distant, you say, إِلَيْهِ, without ا. (Msb.) And أَهْوَى إِلى سَيْفِهِ He reached his sword; took it with his hand, or with his extended hand; or took hold of it. (Msb.) And أَهْوَيْتُ بِالشَّىْءِ [in my copy of the Msb, erroneously, إِلَى الشَّىْءِ ] I made a sign with the thing. (As, S.)
تَهَوَّهَ: see آهَةٌ, in art. اوه.
اِنْهَوَى: see اِنْغَوَى, in art. غو.
هَاهْ and هَاهُ: see آهِ, in art. اوه.

الهَوَى Love, and attachment: then, inclination of the soul, or mind, to a thing: then, blameable inclination; as when one says, اِتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ [ He followed his evil inclination ]; and هُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الأَهْوَآءِ [see below]. (Msb.) See also حُبٌّ. هَوًى Also signifies Beloved [or an object of love ]. (K, Ham, p. 546.) [Being originally an inf. n., it may be used alike as sing. and pl. See an ex. in a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. زين: and see an ex. voce شَكْلٌ.

هُوَّةٌ A deep hollow in the ground: (S, JK, M, Msb, K:) or a hollow, or cavity, in the ground; a pit: (Msb:) or a descent in the ground: (K:) or a deep hollow, cavity, or pit; as also: or a low, or depressed, place in the ground. (TA.) إِجْعَلِ الأَمْرَ هُوَّةً وَاحِدَةٌ Make thou the affair, or case, [ uniform, or] one uniform thing. (Fr in TA, in art. بأج.)
هَوَآءٌ A vacancy; a vacuity; a vacant, or an empty, space. (Mgh.) A vacant, or an empty, thing. (Msb.)
هَوِىٌّ and هُوِىٌّ: see 4, (last sentence), in art. سلم.
هَاوَنٌ, said to be thus, with fet-h to the و, originally هَاوُونٌ, [ A mortar; ] the thing in which one pounds, or bruises: pl. هَوَاوِينُ. (Msb.)
هَاوِيَةٌ An abyss; a depth, or deep place, of which the bottom cannot be reached. (JK, TA.)
مَهْوَى الرَّكِيَّةِ [ The cavity of the well ]. (K, voce إِزَآءٌ.) See مَهْوَاةٌ.
مَهْوَاةٌ: see هُوَّةٌ. The space between two mountains; (S, Msb;) and the like; as also: (S:) a pit, or hollow, dug, or excavated. (Msb.)
مُهَيَّأٌ i. q. زَُمَاوَرْدٌ. (MF, art. ورد.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
